cac:ProcurementProject.cbc:Name: 25/46871 Driving ramps
cac:ProcurementProject.cbc:Description: The Norwegian Labour and Welfare Administration, c/o the Nav Finance and Management Department, the Procurement Section, hereafter called the contracting authority, invites tenderers to an open tender contest in connection with the procurement of threshold eliminators, portable ramps and portable rails, with the accompanying accessories and spare parts. The aim of the procurement is to establish a assortment of threshold eliminators, portable ramps and portable rails, with a width that covers the majority of the needs of the relevant users. The tender competition is divided into sub-contracts in order to in the best possible way cover the needs of the relevant user groups, ensure comparable products and contribute to achieving the desired breadth of assortment. Contracts will be signed for each sub-contract with a sufficient number of tenderers to cover the majority of the users ́needs. The maximum total value is estimated to be up to 25% higher than the estimated total value. Further content of the procurement is specified in the tender documentation.

cac:PresentationPeriod.cbc:Description: Not set separate internal deadlines at the current time.

cac:ProcurementProject.cbc:Name: 1 Threshold eliminator - driving from one side, for indoor and limited outdoor use
cac:ProcurementProject.cbc:Description: Threshold eliminator - driving from one side, for indoor and limited outdoor use, with the accompanying accessories and spare parts. Type of contract: A decision has not been made as to whether parallel framework agreements will be signed or an agreement with one tenderer. Only the tender letter shall be submitted under sub-contract 1-5 (cf. Part I Terms point 3.5). The tender letter and other documentation shall be submitted in sub-contract "Tender Submission".

cac:ContractExtension.cbc:OptionsDescription: The contracting authority has an option for an extension(s) for all or parts of the contract for a period of up to 2 years, cf. Part II the Framework Agreement, point 1.5.
